advances: Ordinary planar cap and section data. The band width is existential and no mixed coarea weight conclusion is asserted.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Under an affine coordinate change with invertible linear part $L$, normals transform contragrediently, so their thresholds are unchanged. The areas $k,Q_i$ and the coareas $\sigma_i$ all multiply by $|\det L|$. For the coarea claim one may disintegrate planar area along the unchanged scalar threshold: the area between thresholds is the integral of the coarea lengths, and the interior coarea length is continuous in the threshold by planar convexity. Thus $q_i,f_i,\Phi_i$ are unchanged. A common positive rescaling of the normals scales each $\sigma_i$ inversely and $M$ directly, also preserving every $f_i$.

If no band exists, for each positive integer $m$ take a counterexample with $\max_i q_i\le4/9+1/m$ and either a row above $2$ or a nontriangular body with a row at least $2$. In each body take a maximum-area inscribed triangle, which exists by continuity on the compact triple product and has positive area. Normalize it affinely to the reference triangle $T_{\rm ref}=\operatorname{conv}((0,0),(1,0),(0,1))$. Each normalized body contains $T_{\rm ref}$, and its maximal triangle area is $1/2$. The normalized bodies are uniformly bounded since replacing vertex $i$ by a point $x$ gives triangle area $|\lambda_i(x)|/2$, where $\lambda_i$ is the reference barycentric coordinate. Hence $|\lambda_i(x)|\le1$ for every $i$. A Hausdorff subsequence converges to a convex body $K_*$ containing the reference triangle. This follows also by uniform subsequential convergence of the uniformly bounded, equi-Lipschitz support functions on the unit circle. Approximating each limit-body vertex of an inscribed triangle by points of the normalized bodies shows that the maximum inscribed area in $K_*$ is still $1/2$. The marks have a subsequence tending to $y_*\in K_*$.

For the transformed normals use $u_i^m=v_i^m/\lVert v_i^m\rVert$ and $a_i^m=\lVert v_i^m\rVert/\sum_j\lVert v_j^m\rVert$. Pass to subsequential limits $u_i,a_i$ of the unit normals and their weights. Then $\sum_i a_i u_i=0$ and $\sum_i a_i=1$. The cap fractions converge to those for $K_*,y_*,u_i$ by dominated convergence away from the limit-body boundary and the limiting cutting lines. Indeed the body indicators converge at every interior and exterior point by Hausdorff convergence and full dimensionality, all bodies lie in one bounded set, and their areas are at least $1/2$. The limiting fractions are at most $4/9$. A single positive balance weight is impossible. If there are exactly two positive weights, their unit vectors are opposite and their caps through $y_*$ have fractions summing to one, impossible. If all three directions were collinear, positive balance would again give an opposite pair. Thus the limit spans the plane and all weights are positive. Any two $a_i u_i$ are linearly independent, since otherwise their negative sum would also be collinear with them.

Let $g$ be the centroid of $K_*$. The classical planar Grünbaum inequality gives area fraction at least $4/9$ for any cap through $g$. If $u_i\cdot(g-y_*)>0$, the cap through $y_*$ strictly exceeds the corresponding cap through $g$ by a positive-area strip, since $g$ is interior. This contradicts the ceiling. Thus all three margins are nonpositive, and their positive balanced sum is zero, so they all vanish. Spanning gives $y_*=g$ and every limiting cap is an equality cap. The classical fixed-direction equality theorem makes $K_*$ a triangle, with the equality cut parallel to an edge. The cap is the apex side, since the apex side of a centroid cut parallel to the base has fraction $4/9$ and the other side $5/9$. The three equality caps isolate distinct vertices: repeated equality directions would force the third direction to be opposite by balance. Since $K_*$ is itself a triangle containing $T_{\rm ref}$ and has maximal inscribed triangle area $1/2$, it equals $T_{\rm ref}$. [Marín Sola and Yepes Nicolás, *On Grünbaum type inequalities*, (1.1) and its equality characterization](https://webs.um.es/jesus.yepes/publicaciones_files/paper_grunbaum.pdf).

Put $w_i^m=a_i^m u_i^m$, which is a common positive rescaling of the three transformed normals, and let $L_m$ be the matrix with first and second rows $(w_1^m)^{\mathsf T},(w_2^m)^{\mathsf T}$. It converges to an invertible $L_*$. Under $x\mapsto L_m(x-y_m)$ the normals become exactly $(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)$ by balance. The bodies converge to $L_*(T_{\rm ref}-g)$ with these fixed normals and source zero. Their limit is a strict distinct-vertex triangle, so the full local convex-body theorem applies for all sufficiently large $m$, with strictness for nontriangles. Affine and common-scale invariance contradict the offending row property. This proves the stated positive band.
statement: There exists a universal $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that the following holds. Let $K$ be a planar convex body, let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$, and take three nonzero spanning normals $v_1+v_2+v_3=0$. For their closed through-$y$ caps write $Q_i=|K\cap\{v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0\}|$, $k=|K|$, $q_i=Q_i/k$, and $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap\{v_i\cdot(x-y)=0\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$. With $M=\sum_iQ_i/\sigma_i$, set $f_i=2\sqrt{kQ_i}/(\sigma_i M)$ and $\Phi_i=f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4$ for distinct indices. If every $q_i\le4/9+\varepsilon_0$, then every $\Phi_i\le2$. For every nontriangular $K$ in this band every row is strict.
title: A positive ordinary cap-ceiling band for the exact Lorentz rows
